newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY JANUARY REAL WAGES UP 6.7 PCT YR/YR.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY JANUARY REAL WAGES UP 6.7 PCT YR/YR.

text.p: Hungary's real wages rose 6.7 percent in the 12 months to January as a result of 24.9 percent rise in net nominal wages on January 1996 and a 18.9 percent year-on-year increase in consumer prices in the same period.
The figures are for full-time employees in firms employing more than 10 in the competitive sector, and do not cover agriculture, the Central Statistical Office (KSH) reported on Friday.
Wages in January are usually strongly up partly because of adjustments to last year's inflation take place, KSH reported.
Including agriculture, net wages averaged 34,537 forints and gross wage averaged 50,667 forints in January.
The highest average net wage, 56,980 forints, was in the financial services sector, a 39.7pc increase on January 1996, followed by the chemicals industry, 48,029 forints, up 31 percent.
